name: thin-results
about: Results exist but each rests on one or two leads: too thin to steer by.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook straight_talk (straight talk) and scene cab_pov (from the cab) spent $41.20 in the last 28 days over 3010 impressions and brought 1 lead, $41.20 per lead.
Our ads with hook proof (proof) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $38.75 in the last 28 days over 2890 impressions and brought 2 leads, $19.38 per lead.

output.audience: Class A drivers who meet the experience requirement and run flatbed, or are ready to. They likely spend longer stretches out now and want a steadier week. A regional job that is home weekly would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a flatbed rolling on Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: The pay per mile is the most concrete fact on the sheet and has not been tried as a lead here. Nothing has been measured for this hook or for formats.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly: the street the driver comes back to at the end of a regional week.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on regional Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home weekly is what sets a regional job apart for a driver who is out longer now. Nothing has been measured for this hook or for formats.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, shown parked with its flatbed trailer, as the driver's own to run.
angles.proof: The job comes with an assigned truck and the work is flatbed.
angles.why: Earlier ads with a truck at rest had the lower cost per lead, but on very few leads and under another hook, so this is thin. Nothing has been measured on formats.

angles.idea: Say plainly who the job is for: Class A drivers who meet the experience requirement, in a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: The opening states its experience requirement and is a Class A regional job in a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: This pair's earlier result is thin: very few leads at a higher cost per lead than our other ads. Stating the requirement plainly gives it a different try. Nothing has been measured on formats.

angles.idea: Set out the job's stated terms as a plain list: pay per mile, home weekly, retirement plan.
angles.proof: The job's facts state the pay per mile, home weekly and a retirement plan.
angles.why: The proof hook had the lower cost per lead of the earlier ads, though on very few leads and with another picture, so it is thin. Nothing has been measured on formats.
